correctness.rationale: For any D,r>0 and deterministic 0<|a|<1 the stationary characteristic product gives arbitrary polynomial Fourier moments. This proves global smoothness and validates the stationary pantograph equation. Iterating its even derivative recurrence gives f^(2n)(0)=(-1)^n f(0)ell^(-2n)c^(-n^2) product_(j<n)(1-c^(2j+1)), f^(2n+1)(0)=0. The product converges to a positive limit, implying exp(L n^2+O(n)) derivative growth, zero Taylor radius and failure of all finite Gevrey bounds. The known absolutely convergent exponential series is holomorphic in either open half-plane. Positive Fourier weight and the global cosine remainder yield the exact Taylor error <= f(0) exp(L-(log(ell/abs(x)))^2/L) when n=floor(log(ell/abs(x))/L)>=1. The packaged checker independently passed 202 finite tests; no infinite inference rests on tests.

value.rationale: The exact stationary law is used to infer a Gaussian-like central core in proportional-reset diffusion. The theorem explains the otherwise puzzling joint presence of global smoothness and Taylor divergence at its physically distinguished reset point, quantifies a new all-order derivative growth law and gives a usable superalgebraic local approximation with truncation order scaling as log(1/abs(x)). The object and invariant arise naturally from the motivating model and are not an arbitrary finite numerical slice.
